citations.review_text: Problems with the gamepad. The settings change over time and it is impossible to play.

FIFA is as boring as ever.
This is the first title I've played since FIFA 19, and well...it sucks.
Nothing feels like its changed, except for the shiny UI underneath which everything is much the same.

At least FIFA 19 had the "Hunter" mode, which was cool.

And to make things worse, they've made defending crap, at least Legacy defending, CPU AI players simply zip past if you're out of position and there is really nothing you can do as you watch them score that inevitable goal.
The best way to make this game a little playable is to mess with the User/CPU performance sliders, switch to tactical defending, and invest in a good CDM and hold the shape of your back 5.

What a disappointment.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the PC version was missing the new-generation HyperMotion technology feature present on PS5 and Xbox Series consoles.

citations.review_text:
If you thought the PC community was angry about FIFA 21, FIFA 22 took that frustration and amplified it. Despite PC hardware being more than capable, EA once again decided to treat PC players as an afterthought, delivering the old-generation version of the game while hyping up their new HyperMotion technology exclusively for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series consoles.

Let that sink in: if you bought this on Steam, you were paying full price for a game that was intentionally missing the biggest marketing feature of the year. It was essentially FIFA 21.5 with updated kits and rosters, making the PC player base feel completely disrespected.

As for the actual gameplay we got on PC, it was a very strange mixed bag. The goalkeepers were buffed to an absurd level inside the penalty box, making point-blank saves look like scenes from an action movie. Yet, ironically, you could score finesse shots from 30 yards out with incredible ease. The pace-abuse meta was slightly toned down compared to the previous year, giving passers a bit more room to breathe, but the notorious momentum shifts and heavy scripting were still glaringly present.

 Competitive matches often felt like they were decided by the game engine rather than pure skill.

For offline players, Career Mode introduced the Create a Club feature. It was a step in the right direction and fun for a few seasons, allowing you to design your own kits and stadium, but it ultimately lacked the deep, immersive customization needed to keep it engaging long-term. 

Ultimate Team, as expected, remained the primary focus of the developers, continuing its aggressive trend of heavy monetization and pay-to-win mechanics disguised behind shiny weekly promos.

Objectively speaking, looking at the overwhelming community consensus, it was a deeply disappointing port for the PC platform. It functions as a decent football game if you just want to kick a ball around offline or play locally with friends, but the decision to deny PC players the…

FIFA 22 makes a noticeable leap in realism thanks to HyperMotion technology, which brings smoother animations and more natural player movement—especially on next-gen consoles. Gameplay feels more tactical, with slower build-up play, improved ball physics, and more authentic goalkeeping. Career Mode and Pro Clubs got meaningful updates, adding depth for offline and co-op fans.

However, FIFA Ultimate Team remains weighed down by microtransactions and a heavy grind, which overshadows its otherwise engaging modes. While not a revolutionary entry, it delivers a polished football experience that balances authenticity with accessibility.

FIFA 22 is yet another disappointing entry in the long-running series. While the visuals are polished and the gameplay feels smooth at times, these positives are overshadowed by a mountain of flaws that make the game frustrating and unenjoyable.

The AI is as frustrating as ever, with defenders often standing around cluelessly and attackers making nonsensical runs. Tackling feels pointless, as the ball frequently bounces back to the opposition, and the randomness of gameplay moments makes it feel like skill has little to do with success. Goalkeepers are either superhuman or completely useless, with no middle ground, leading to inconsistent and infuriating matches.

Career Mode, a staple for many players, remains stagnant and outdated. The menus are clunky and slow, the design is uninspired, and the features feel like they've been copy-pasted from previous decades. Transfers are unrealistic, training is boring, and the lack of meaningful updates makes the mode feel like an afterthought.

The introduction of HyperMotion technology was hyped as a game-changer, but in reality, it adds little to the experience. The animations are often awkward, and the gameplay still suffers from the same issues that have plagued the series for years.

On top of all this, the game is riddled with microtransactions. Ultimate Team continues to prioritize monetization over player enjoyment, with endless packs and overpriced items that make the mode feel like a cash grab. The focus on cosmetics, like countless kits and stadium customizations, feels excessive and unnecessary.

Overall, FIFA 22 is a prime example of EA's complacency and focus on profit over quality. It's a game that looks good on the surface but fails to deliver a satisfying football experience. Longtime fans of the series deserve better.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the gameplay as feeling scripted and artificial.

citations.review_text:
Wanted to enjoy FIFA 22 but it’s a massive disappointment. Ultimate Team is pure pay-to-win; you either spend real money or get crushed by those who do. The scripting is obvious and infuriating — momentum swings and ridiculous goals ruin every match.

Gameplay feels stiff and repetitive, Career Mode is boring and outdated, and the whole thing lacks soul. Years later, it just feels abandoned.

The last okay football game from EA. I love these types of football games, but there are no good options right now. The gameplay feels too scripted and artificial, and the newer games are even worse in that regard, which makes it tiring real fast. I still play it, but mostly in short bursts with months between sessions.

it's a pretty trash game and feels scripted at times but i will be very honest that i had the most fun out of this game.
When i was stuck in TARC ( Residential Campus ) of my university this game had us play 2v2 and it was the only FIFA that could run on my laptop. the 2v2 sessions were really fun and unforgettable, I will thank the game for being a very important part of my memory.
